title: Keep the stationary reversal boundary when hiding finite-window dissipation
statement: For every finite irreducible n-state Q, finite T and positive delta,eta, the reviewed fourfold lift is irreducible with4n hidden states, one fixed common escape clock and passive full-path TV error<=delta while sustained reversal divergence rate<eta. Its stationary path KL is B+T sigma. The orientation bit has B=(1-2epsilon)log((1-epsilon)/epsilon), possibly unbounded, while its KL to an unbiased bit is at most log2.

requires: Finite irreducible source Q and actual reversal/observation interface
provides: A compatible passive coarse-path completion and a counterexample to rate inference from fixed clock/window alone
assumptions: The lift uses asymmetric stationary preparation and arbitrarily slow orientation relaxation
Unbounded B is not unbounded stored bits, work or necessary preparation time
A supplied Bmax restores [I_T-Bmax]+/T; visible decay/irreducibility/clock ceilings alone do not acquire a uniform hidden-memory-erasure promise
This does not turn arbitrary data into exact parity-invariant equilibrium or preserve a resolved singleton-port reset
costs: Pay observation/record integrals, stationary preparation, small weights/switch rates and hidden mixing; a fixed escape ceiling does not bound them
Tree LP tables, confidence coverage, dovetailed revisits and all hidden states/rates of approximation remain unbounded resources
Native flux E, E/R per departure and E/W per physical time must keep their separate normalization
contract.units: Stationary path KL B+T sigma, full-path total variation, rate per source time and one orientation bit; no automatic thermodynamic work conversion.
contract.obstruction: Finite-window irreversibility can reside in a stationary reversal-preparation boundary rather than a large sustained rate.
